text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained 0.7% today to close at $424.89, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that has added nearly 10% to its price. The core driver is the escalating Middle East conflict: Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure are intensifying, and the State Department warned Americans against travel to the region. These geopolitical risks are tightening global oil supplies, pushing world crude to $130.80 per barrel—well above the U.S. price of $107—and refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, a very high utilization rate that amplifies refinery profits when oil supplies feel constrained.

The timing matters: U.S. refiners like Marathon benefit directly when Middle East turmoil disrupts supply flows, because they can process available crude at wider profit margins. The market's concern that Saudi pipeline damage "is less disruptive than feared" (from September 18) briefly capped the rally, but ongoing Strait closure and fresh attacks around Riyadh's airport have kept energy prices elevated, supporting the refiner's stock push higher through the week.
